guarantees.claim: For indices i from KeyMgrStages to 2**StageWidth-1, id_matrix[i] is assigned to the replication of data_rand[0] IdLfsrCopies times.

uncertain_points.claim: If KeyMgrStages >= 2**StageWidth, the generate loop produces no assignments, leaving parts of id_matrix undriven.
uncertain_points.risk: Undriven id_matrix entries could be read as X or unpredictable values, leading to functional errors or security weakness.

formal_sketch.consequent: the generate loop produces no assignments, leaving parts of id_matrix undriven

uncertain_points.claim: All bits of id_matrix[i] are set to the same value data_rand[0], drastically reducing per-entry entropy.
uncertain_points.cond: always when the generate loop synthesizes
uncertain_points.risk: If id_matrix is used for key mixing or masking, the constant-bit pattern may enable predictable secret extraction or linear attacks.

formal_sketch.antecedent: always when the generate loop synthesizes
formal_sketch.consequent: All bits of id_matrix[i] are set to the same value data_rand[0], drastically reducing per-entry entropy

security_implications: id_matrix entries are formed by replicating data_rand[0] IdLfsrCopies times, so every bit in an entry is identical. This drastically limits randomness independent of the source quality. If id_matrix participates in key derivation or any masking operation, the lack of intra-word entropy could make secrets predictable or vulnerable to side-channel analysis.
